content:
Hey, some more news from the industry, admittedly done aeons ago (leanprover/lean4:nightly-2023-06-10 :scream:), but only very recently open-sourced :).

The folks at RISC Zero have an implementation of RISC-V as a zero knowledge circuit (read: a huge pile of polynomial constraints) and we (Nethermind) wrote some Lean to reason about their infrastructure. Proved some POCs, perhaps most interestingly that the giant pile of constraints that is supposed to be the instruction decoder for the RISC-V ISA does in fact correctly decode instructions :).
Discussions about this happen at #general > Discussion: RISC-V verification
